fact: Togo First says Togo AI Lab is developing models that understand and generate content in several Togolese languages, within a national local-languages project using LLMs, RAG and AI agents.

Togo AI Lab, with Zindi and the Togolese startup Umbaji, is building an open-source platform to collect voice and text data, aiming for at least 50 hours of validated recordings and 6,000 translated sentence pairs for each of 50 national languages, to train speech recognition, speech synthesis and translation models, as presented at AI for Good in July 2026.

fact: Google.org's $2 million support will give University of Lomé and University of Kara faculty and students access to high performance computer clusters under the Togo Data Lab, run by CEGA and the Ministry of Public Service Efficiency and Digital Transformation.
UNDP says it deployed country-hosted AI compute capacity in Togo under its AI Infrastructure Activation programme.
UNDP's programme procured and deployed country-hosted GPU compute in Togo.
The GSMA and the governments of Benin, Kenya, Namibia, Nigeria and Togo launched ATLAS Umoja AI to build AI models for African languages, with private partners Awarri, Zindi, Pawa AI and Mozisha.

Agence Ecofin reports that Togo's ministry of public service efficiency and digital transformation, under minister Cina Lawson, officially launched in early October 2026 the three-year 'Voix du Togo' programme collecting voice and text data in Ewe, Kabiye and Moba (targets per language: 50 hours of validated audio, 6,000 translated sentence pairs, 500 speakers) to train AI models.
The Togo Data Lab, working with CEGA, is developing a satellite-imagery and AI project with the Ministry of Agriculture using MOSAIKS tools, and the lab has grown to more than 20 data scientists.
